mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each director's and UBO's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or Consular Office of the individual's home government
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization at nearest Canadian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of current residential address of UBO (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility supplier or account-holding financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity and source of funds of UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified financial institution in UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: PEP and sanctions self-declaration form (signed under oath)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or lawyer in the UBO's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), UK HMT and EU consolidated lists where applicable, and FINTRAC AML/CFT guidelines. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign), with written source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis and six-year record retention.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry via BC OnLine (https://www.bconline.gov.bc.ca/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English or French using Roman letters, numerals, and permitted punctuation; non-Roman scripts must be transliterated to an approved Latin-character form. A distinct element and a legal element (Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limited) are mandatory. The name must not misrepresent the nature, quality, or jurisdiction of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies through BC OnLine within 30 days, attaching a corrected Name Request, explanatory grounds, and any regulatory consents. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file a petition for declaratory relief and judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, no later than 60 days following the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible if they provide a physical street address in BC, an agent present at that address during business hours, and a records office where the transparency register and statutory records are available for inspection. Mail-forwarding-only services or post-office box addresses are not permissible because service of process and record production obligations cannot be met.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: for a non-licensed software and application provider, the expected probability of an unannounced on-site inspection is below 5% annually. The British Columbia Registrar may verify a registered office by mail or telephone; however, CRA or FINTRAC may conduct an on-site records examination during an audit, which is generally scheduled rather than spontaneous.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory processing tariff per BC OnLine fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended hourly rate / fixed incorporation flat fee benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (BCA) — s. 10 (incorporation instrument), s. 12 (certificate of incorporation), s. 44 (incorporation report), s. 201 (written resolutions), s. 226 (corporate records), s. 227 (share consideration), s. 232 (registered office), s. 252 (share structure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online), Service BC, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 3) filed electronically together with Notice of Articles (Form 2) and Notice of Directors (Form 1) under s. 10 of the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: British Columbia prescribes no minimum paid-up share capital for a business corporation; s. 227 BCA permits directors to issue shares for any consideration they determine. No escrow account, capital deposit, or bank block account is required at formation, and the company may commence operations with nominal issued capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporator subscribes for and is allotted 1,000 common shares at CAD $0.01 per share, fully paid and non-assessable; (2) the registered and records office is established at 888 Dunsmuir Street, Suite 900, Vancouver, BC V6C 3K4, Canada, and Corporate Registry Service Ltd. is appointed as registered office agent; (3) the Company adopts its Articles and By-Law No. 1; (4) Jordan M. Chen is appointed sole director, Michael R. Wright Chief Executive Officer, and Sarah K. Li Chief Financial Officer; and (5) the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, register the Company with the Canada Revenue Agency, and complete municipal business licence filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Approval via NUANS Search and Reservation Request
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online portal (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca), Service BC, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online using a BC Services Card or registered account; complete the Name Reservation Request with the proposed legal name; the system generates a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report against the Canadian corporate database; pay the non-refundable name search fee; upon approval, the name is reserved for 56 days, within which the Incorporation Application must be filed. Alternatively, the company may proceed as a numbered company without a name reservation.
required_dossiers: Consent of individual where a personal name is proposed
Authorized signatory identification for Corporate Online login
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the registry notice sets out the grounds; the applicant may file a revised Name Reservation Request with a new distinctive element or request a discretionary name approval with supporting justification. The search fee is not refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application Package (Forms 1, 2 and 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online; also accepted at Service BC service counters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application (Form 3) stating the company name or incorporation number, the Notice of Articles (Form 2) setting out the authorized share structure (unlimited common shares without par value) and any special rights, and the Notice of Directors (Form 1) listing each director's full legal name, residential address and citizenship; attach the signed Articles or adopt the Model Articles by reference; pay the incorporation fee of CAD $350 online; the registrar verifies compliance with s. 10 BCA and issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the incorporation number.
required_dossiers: Notice of Directors (Form 1) with director consents
Registered office and records office address in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction notice, the applicant must amend the electronic forms and cure the defect within the stated period, generally 14 days. If left uncorrected, the application is returned and the incorporation fee refunded, while the name reservation may be extended or renewed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Business Number, Corporate Tax, GST/HST and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (bro.cra.gc.ca) and CRA Business Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, register with the CRA through Business Registration Online or by telephone using Form RC1; the CRA issues a nine-digit Business Number with program accounts: corporate income tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), and payroll (RP); GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable worldwide revenues exceed CAD $30,000 or voluntary to claim input tax credits; obtain a BC PST ruling from the BC Ministry of Finance on whether the SaaS portfolio-tracking subscription is non-taxable remote software access; file the election for a fiscal year-end and confirm the filing schedule.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 or online business registration application
Directors' personal identification and residency evidence
First Board Resolution authorizing tax registrations
Financial institution details for tax account direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries or suspends the application, the director may correct the filing through CRA My Business Account or call the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525; submitting the written board resolution, Certificate of Incorporation and director identification within the response window normally reinstates the registration without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Report to Prevent Administrative Dissolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months of the date of incorporation, file the Incorporation Report required by s. 44 BCA; confirm the current directors, registered office and records office details, and pay the applicable registry fee; the report is a mandatory pre-dissolution form and keeps the company in good standing; the registrar will not dissolve a company with a filed incorporation report.
required_dossiers: Updated Notice of Directors if there has been a change since incorporation
Registered office and records office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the report is rejected for inaccurate director information or address details, refile the corrected electronic report before the two-month deadline; the registrar stays dissolution while the correction is pending. Late filing exposes the company to administrative dissolution and a restoration proceeding under the BCA, requiring a court-free reinstatement application and payment of arrears.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Resolution and Corporate Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (internal corporate act; no government filing at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain the sole director's unanimous written resolution under s. 201(1) BCA; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription and allotment, registered office adoption, officer appointments and banking authorities; approve By-Law No. 1, authorize the issuing of share certificates, open the share register, and set the fiscal year-end; maintain the corporate records book, including the register of directors and share register, at the records office in British Columbia as required under s. 226 BCA.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and officer consent letters
Registered office and records office notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer appointment is invalid due to lack of consent or non-execution, the deficiency can be cured by a ratification written resolution, with all consents signed and back-dated to the effective appointment date; failure to maintain records is remedied by immediate preparation and filing of the statutory registers to avoid offences under s. 226 BCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, WorkSafeBC Registration and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or applicable BC municipality); WorkSafeBC; the Company's appointed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence covering software publishing activity (NAICS 511210 / ISIC 6201) at the corporate office; supply the landlord's consent and the fire-safety clearance; register as an employer with WorkSafeBC if the company has employees, or file a clearance notification where the sole director is excluded; execute the banking resolution and open the corporate operating account; implement a PIPEDA-compliant privacy program for financial portfolio data because the cloud application processes personal financial information; note that no sectoral licence from the BC Financial Services Authority is required because the company does not carry on regulated deposit-taking, dealing or advisory activities.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening resolution and officer identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the licence due to zoning, apply for a temporary use permit or relocate to a commercial-office zoned premise; if WorkSafeBC assigns an incorrect industry classification, appeal to the Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal; if the bank requests additional due diligence, provide a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, the board resolution, and beneficial-owner identification to complete the account activation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 software publishing and cloud portfolio-tracking services. The applicable approval authority is the City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or the relevant BC municipality) acting under the Community Charter, S.B.C. 2003, c. 26, supplemented by WorkSafeBC for occupational safety registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (general occupation licence for software development and cloud application services); no provincial manufacturing, operating, or financial-sector permit is required for the fintech portfolio analytics activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office, BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (provincial); Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal, Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA Required. Software publishing and cloud data services are not listed as reviewable projects under the Reviewable Projects Regulation, B.C. Reg. 250/2019 of the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 51. No registration, environmental certificate, or self-assessment is triggered for this activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions arise from cloud-based software operations. General compliance: electronic waste consisting of servers, computers and hardware must be managed through a registered stewardship program under the Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 449/2004; HVAC refrigerants must meet the Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations (SOR/2016-137); office wastewater must conform to municipal sewer bylaws, notably the Vancouver Sewer and Drainage By-law 8099 applicable limits for BOD, suspended solids and pH. Negligible VOC emissions are limited to cleaning agents and printing supplies and must remain within the provincial OHS indoor-air screening levels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: compliance certificate under the BC Fire Code, B.C. Reg. 215/2018, covering fire alarms, extinguishers, exit signage and an evacuation plan for the commercial office. Structural load and occupancy: building permit and occupancy clearance under the Vancouver Building By-law 1257 for the leased Class A office. Occupational clearance: WorkSafeBC registration and compliance with the Workers Compensation Act, R.S.B.C. 2019, c. 1 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, including ergonomic workstation, electrical safety, and emergency preparedness requirements for all personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident corporations file Form RC1 (or RC1A) with CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN); activate corporate income tax program account RC0001 and GST/HST program account RT0001. Register separately with BC Ministry of Finance (eTaxBC) for PST if making taxable sales in BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box/pass-through election for Canadian corporations. Hybrid mismatch rules (sections 18.2/18.21 ITA) govern dual-consistency and deduction/non-inclusion outcomes; treaty relief and subsection 85 rollover elections remain separately available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (or a single calendar quarter) triggers mandatory GST/HST registration; BC PST registration is required from the first taxable sale in BC (no threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping at federal level. CRA accepts electronic records; GST/HST invoices must contain prescribed statutory particulars. Pan-Canadian Peppol e-invoicing is voluntary; BC PST returns are filed via eTaxBC, without API-mandated fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when exported by the supplier in a commercial transaction or shipped to a foreign addressee under a bill of lading. Services and intangible supplies (including subscription cloud analytics) are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and where the supply is not performed on Canadian real or tangible personal property. Evidence must show the non-resident's status and the destination/use outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Cargo Export Declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment proof of foreign currency proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA can reassess beyond the normal 4-year limitation period for misrepresentation, claw back refunds/input tax credits, impose penalties (5% of misreported tax under ETA s. 280; up to 50% for gross negligence) and institute criminal proceedings for intentional evasion; directors and controlling officers may be held personally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and cross-border funds-flow monitoring by FINTRAC; Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange administration, foreign-exchange policy being administered by the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act and the Financial Administration Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible. Canada maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime with no capital or current account restrictions, no FX licensing, and no general profit-remittance approval. Dividends to non-residents may be repatriated freely but are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory rate, reduced under applicable tax treaties) and require NR4 reporting to the CRA. SaaS export revenue, royalty and share-redemption proceeds face no currency rationing or conversion hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian exporters and SaaS vendors are not required to surrender export proceeds, convert receipts within a statutory timeline, or maintain a minimum conversion ratio. Foreign-currency receipts may be held offshore; however, for tax purposes all revenue must be measured in CAD unless the corporation validly elects a functional currency under Income Tax Act section 261, and the Bank of Canada exchange rate must be documented for each transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) with treasury and FX desks; capital escrow not applicable at incorporation
Operating Account (CAD) plus USD clearing account and commercial card merchant settlement
Operating Account (CAD/USD) with cross-border cash management; inclusion in BMO Global Trade Services for documentary credits
Operating Account (CAD) and CIBC Smart Business account for fintech vendor settlements
Operating Account (CAD) with Pacific-business corridor expertise and Latin/Asia payment connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low–Medium. The European-style electronic-money institution (EMI) has no direct Canadian statutory analogue; an offshore EMI cannot lawfully take deposits, issue electronic money, or hold client balances in the Canadian market without becoming a bank or a licensed MSB. Given the entity is a pure SaaS analytics platform (ISIC 6201, no required statutory license), an offshore EMI is not advisable commercially and should be replaced by a Canadian tier-1 bank account coupled with regulated PSP payment acceptance (Stripe, Apple IAP). Any holding of third-party funds or unlicensed money transmission would trigger the Bank Act banking privilege and FINTRAC MSB registration requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permissible in Canada; physical branch attendance is not mandatory. Tier-1 banks require, at minimum, a secure video-call interview of at least one director/signing officer and all 25%-and-over beneficial owners under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC client-identification rules, a certified copy of the BC company registry extract, a directors' resolution authorizing account opening, and proof of registered office address. A notarized corporate packet executed by Canadian legal counsel is routinely accepted as the standard evidentiary bundle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity, including multi-tier share structures or offshore nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Registry extract showing shareholders and directors; organizational chart; share register and share subscription agreements; passport and proof-of-residence of each beneficial owner; signed senior-management declaration on source of wealth/funds

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders connected with higher-risk jurisdictions (including China-sourced shareholders)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports, visa/residence permits, original bank reference letters from the remitting institution, source-of-funds documentation (bank statements over 12 months), third-party sanctions/PEP screening report, and a corporate-law legal opinion confirming foreign-direct-investment clearance or exemption under the Investment Canada Act

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fintech business classification as unregistered money services business or payment aggregator
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming the non-custodial SaaS nature; master SaaS agreement and terms-of-use; revenue flow model showing subscription/licence fees only; evidence that Stripe and Apple act as regulated PSPs and payment facilitators; FINTRAC non-registration letter or MSB exemption memo

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, rapid inbound capital injections from foreign shareholders shortly after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Term sheet and capitalization table; board minutes authorizing share issuance; wire instruction/purpose code tied to share subscription; valuation memorandum; originating bank SWIFT advisements; downstream allocation plan for treasury funds

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliance protocol: route inbound funds exclusively as SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit transfers to the designated CAD operating account, with a purpose code mapping to equity subscription (OECD transaction code 5120 is standard, while Canadian banks accept domestic code 009). FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer (EFT) reporting is triggered on all cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in relevant scenarios; the company must retain the share subscription agreement, board resolution, source-of-funds statements, and the originating bank's reference to demonstrate a lawful non-money-laundering purpose. Funds must be booked as contributed surplus or share capital in the CRA tax filings and do not require Bank of Canada approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements settle over: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-urgent international vendor payments; (ii) Payments Canada Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for institutional CAD wholesale settlements; (iii) Real-Time Rail (RTR) once fully launched for CAD instant payment requests; and (iv) UCP-600 documentary credits via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for high-value hardware/cloud-infrastructure procurement. Standby letters of credit (SWIFT MT760) are available from the tier-1 bank to guarantee SaaS delivery obligations. Stripe and Apple IAP aggregations settle via the PSP's payout cycles into the CAD operating account, with merchant integration governed by those PSPs' commercial terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards under an ISDA/CSA master agreement with the tier-1 bank at maturities up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forwards for restricted or illiquid currencies in intercompany settlement scenarios
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps for multi-currency treasury liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under section 197 of the Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the annual date (anniversary of incorporation, continuation or registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No daily late fee; a default notice may be issued; if annual reports remain unfiled for two consecutive years, the registrar may dissolve the company by administrative strike-off; reinstatement requires arrears filing plus restoration fee. Offence fines of up to CAD 5,000 may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return (only for a company incorporated or continued under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years can lead to dissolution; no automatic administrative strike-off before notice; late filings and reinstatement require the prescribed fee and updated records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including portfolio investment and T1135/T1134 schedules as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; repeated failure can increase the penalty to 10%; CRA may issue demands, garnish assets and assess director liability only for unremitted withholdings, not income tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold requires a statutory audit for a private British Columbia company; an auditor must be appointed at each AGM unless shareholders unanimously waive the appointment. Publicly distributed/reporting issuers and CBCA distributing corporations are mandatory-audit entities; a shareholder holding 5% or more of the voting shares may requisition an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises and reporting issuers apply IFRS as published in the CPA Canada Handbook; private companies may elect Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) for financial reporting, with T2 schedules prepared from the same records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a BC provincial company there is no separate annual UBO filing; share transfers are recorded in the transfer register and confirmed in the annual report only to the extent of director/officer changes. For a CBCA federal company, an Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register must be maintained, any acquisition or cessation of significant control recorded within 15 days, and the ISC information reported annually in the federal annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (CBCA federal companies only)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 400 per year for registered office and records-office agent services in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 22,500 per year for a small private Canadian technology company if a full audit is engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 38% basic rate; effective federal 15% (after Provincial Abatement 10% and General Tax Reduction 13%); British Columbia combined general 27% (Federal +12.0% BC). CCPC active business income up to CAD 500,000: Federal 9% + BC 2.0% = 11.0% combined
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (CCPC, shared CAD 500,000 limit); Canadian-controlled private corporation refundable investment tax mechanism; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) ITC 35%/15%/20% (fintech software qualifies under CRA criteria); BC Digital Entertainment Tax Credit 75% BC labour (principal production nexus in BC); no statutory tax holiday at federal level; 44.7% refundable federal tax on aggregate investment income (CCPC)
